title: streaming lifecycle: robust handling for client cancel/disconnect and reconnect/resume with server timeouts
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: production streaming connections were occasionally leaving in-flight inference work stranded when clients disconnected abruptly or issued explicit cancels. This caused wasted GPU work and inconsistent resume behavior when clients attempted to reconnect. This PR centralizes streaming lifecycle controls: explicit client cancel semantics, improved disconnect handling with graceful server-side abort and reclaim, reconnect/resume token mapping with timebox heuristics, and conservative server-side timeouts to avoid leaking requests. Summary of changes: 1) add ConnectionManager that tracks active streaming sessions, their KV cache state pointers, and cancel tokens; 2) introduce client-initiated CANCEL control message (OpenAI-compat layer accepts a `stop`/`cancel` event) that triggers immediate KV-cache release and best-effort inference abortion; 3) on unexpected disconnect, server starts a reclaim timer (configurable per-tenant) during which a reconnect with resume token can reattach and continue from the same KV state; 4) if reclaim timer expires, server finalizes abort and reclaims resources; 5) implement safe resume semantics in the openai_compat handler: resume token validation, sequence continuity checks, and fallback to restart-generation when mismatch detected; 6) introduce server-side inference soft timeout and a hard preemption path that signals runtime to checkpoint progress before abort to reduce wasted token compute; 7) add exhaustive unit and integration tests exercising cancel/disconnect/reconnect/timeouts and end-to-end examples for SDKs. Backwards compatibility: behavior is additive and opt-in via a per-tenant streaming lifecycle feature flag; existing clients continue to work but will start benefiting from faster reclaim once enabled. Rollout plan: staged feature flag rollout to internal staging, canary on low-traffic production clusters, monitor latency and allocation metrics, then wider rollout. Testing: new unit tests and e2e streaming tests added; CI includes new flaky-tolerant streaming e2e run. See files_changed for details.

review_comments: Diego Morales: Can we make the reclaim timer configurable per-tenant? Some enterprise customers have slower reconnection patterns.
Author (Ava Chen): Yes, added per-tenant reclaim window and a global default in deploy/feature-flags/streaming_lifecycle.yaml.
Priya Nair: How do we ensure resume tokens are not replayed to hijack sessions?
Author (Ava Chen): Resume tokens are single-use and tied to a session id + short TTL; server validates origin and sequence continuity. Added tests for token replay rejection.
Samir Patel: We saw intermittent e2e flakes in streaming tests. Can we retry the flaky test instead of ignoring?
Author (Ava Chen): Added flaky-tolerant re-run logic for the streaming e2e pipeline and instrumented metrics to surface recurrence.
release_notes: Improved streaming lifecycle controls: client-initiated CANCEL support, graceful handling of unexpected disconnects with configurable reclaim window, reconnect/resume semantics with resume token validation, and server-side soft timeouts with preemption hooks to reduce wasted inference work. Opt-in via feature flag; rollout will be canaryed before wide release.
